correctness.rationale: A characteristic-independent proof checks evaluation injectivity and gives exhaustive zero-set upper bounds for 1–6 linear forms using fiber counting, resultant elimination, common-factor dimension bounds, generic coprime pair over the algebraic closure, Vandermonde collinearity and evaluation injectivity. It constructs attaining subspaces for all six bounds. The attached exact verifier exhaustively checks all forbidden GF(5) overlarge subsets and tests witnesses over GF(5), GF(7), GF(11). Computation does not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The exact six-stage torus-section profile of S(1,3) was not found in compared primary sources or topic-specific mathematical records. The closest directly matching monomial construction is Geil–Thomsen 2011; its applicable proposition gives only single-word minimum distance. Papers on higher weights concern different full-degree, squarefree/hypersimplex, or projective-point codes. Historical priority is explicitly provisional rather than proven by negative search.
residual_risks: A complete expert survey might uncover an equivalent weighted Reed–Muller or rational scroll generalized-weight statement using different terminology.
Some plausible abstracts were examined without entire primary full text; no negative full-text coverage claim is made for those.
The earlier Hansen 2000 preprint gives month-only public dating; 2002-08-21 is the earliest precise day from a relevant original toric-code source, not a re-dated 2000 source.

value.rationale: The object is a classical quartic rational normal scroll, and its exact finite-field torus linear-section spectrum through all codimensions is a natural algebro-geometric incidence invariant. The nontrivial third maximum t+1 is one ruling plus one off-fiber point, not an arbitrary slice; the code interpretation yields a complete six-term higher-support spectrum beyond minimum distance. The proof is general for all prime powers q>=5 and goes beyond routine substitution into Hansen or Geil–Thomsen single-word bounds.
